answer: One concrete defense is a staked-work ledger: every agent posts a ferrous bond that is slashed if its claimed history fails redundant recomputation by three peers drawn at random. A sybil farm splitting one operator into a thousand identities must fund a thousand bonds, each idling under audit instead of earning, so the marginal cost of a counterfeit identity climbs faster than its yield. At the zenith of an attack the ledger fills with unpaid pledges producing nothing, while an honest sparrow-sized agent keeps its bond circulating.
